Hi Elaine —

Thanks for the RFI and the clear priority list. We've filled the questionnaire and attached a short summary pack. High‑level points up front:

- Cross-border transfers: Redwood supports a layered approach — SCCs where applicable, DPF compliance controls by default for EU→US flows, and a Private deployment option (VPC or on‑prem) when residency is required.
- KMS: Customer-managed keys are supported via AWS KMS and Google Cloud KMS in our Dedicated and Private offerings; hosted tier supports bring‑your‑own‑KMS for enterprise contracts.
- Retention & deletion: Default behavior for hosted API is not to retain prompts for model training; short‑lived KV/prefix caches are maintained for session performance and are removed within configured windows (default 7 days). We offer configurable retention windows and expedited deletion as a contractual option.
- Logging: Application telemetry is aggregated and redacted by default; request logs capture metadata and usage counters. Raw prompts are not stored for training in hosted by default.
- DPA Annex: Draft DPA Annex (attached) with examples of clauses we typically include for data residency and subprocessors.

Attachments: Redwood_DPF_Answers_20250618.pdf, DPA_Annex_Draft_20250618.docx

We can do a 30‑minute technical call Friday 10:00–10:30am EST. Marissa from Product will join to cover contract and DPA items; David from Infrastructure can join for KMS/residency details.

Next steps suggested:
1) We return the filled RFI (attached) for your review.
2) Schedule Friday call and list 2–3 technical questions you want us to prioritize.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

If you can have David address those two points in the call, that would be ideal. Also, please include any sample language we can circulate to legal regarding deletion SLA (e.g., 24–72 hours expedited deletion if we request).

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Data protection operational questionnaire — technical clarifications

Elaine —

Thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front, followed by brief technical detail you can share with your privacy/legal teams: 

1) Persistence of request payloads (hosted):
- Default hosted behavior: request payloads (prompt + input metadata) are processed in‑memory and streamed to the model runtime. We persist structured request logs (request id, timestamp, model variant, token counts, anonymized metadata) for observability and billing for a default retention of 30 days.
- Raw prompt retention: by default, raw prompts are not kept for model training. We may retain raw request payloads in encrypted storage for a short troubleshooting window (default 7 days) only for requests flagged by system diagnostics or on a sampling basis for quality monitoring.
- Ephemeral/Non‑persisting mode: we support a "no retention" hosted flag for regulated customers (no raw payloads written to disk, logs only contain request ids), available under enterprise contracts with an agreed SLA.

2) Customer‑managed KMS & key access:
- KMS options: AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, and external HSM via KMIP (Dedicated/Private).
- Access model: when customer‑managed keys are used, Redwood operates under an envelope encryption model: data keys are generated and encrypted with the customer key; Redwood does not retain plaintext data keys.
- Support access: Redwood engineers do not have default access to plaintext when CMK is enabled. Emergency access flows (e.g., for incident response) require: documented customer approval, strict access window, and are logged in the audit trail. For on‑prem/private deployments, customers can configure zero‑access patterns.

3) Deletion SLA language (sample):
- Expedited deletion: Redwood will remove request payloads and associated caches within 24 hours of a verified deletion request for accounts on Dedicated or Private plans; for Hosted plans, expedited deletion within 72 hours is available under enterprise agreement.

4) KV/prefix caches & model state:
- KV caches used for session acceleration are retained for configurable windows (default 7 days) and are included in deletion requests. We do not persist model internal weights.
